<!--
  ui-component — the spec for ONE reusable UI component: what it is, when to use it, its anatomy,
  variants, states, configurable API, behavior, and accessibility contract. Text-first.
  Lives at: `design/components/<component-slug>.md` — one page per component; or
    `design/components/<module>/<component-slug>.md` when one module covers every page its `realizes:`
    names, under the deepest such module. A component realizing `[[product:app-base]]`, or pages no one
    module covers, lives at the top level. The page moves (`/wiki-move`) whenever a change to its
    `realizes:` changes that home.
  Authorship: curated. SLO: 180d, AND stale whenever any page `realizes:` names is updated after this one —
    either trigger fires. The timer stays alongside the edge: a component spec can drift from what shipped even
    though the feature it realizes has not changed.
  Owner: fixed to `design`, do not substitute.
  Distinct from: a surface — one addressable screen or view (a page, a modal, a step). A component is
    a reusable part appearing on one. A dialog that is a step in a flow is a surface; a dialog reused
    across features is a component. The feature's `## Surfaces` inventory owns the surface
    vocabulary; this page owns the component.
  Discipline: the visual anatomy and interactive states live in a design tool or project design file
    where one exists (linked, never copied), and in this page's text where none does — this page holds
    the structured spec plus the pointers, not pasted screenshots. Record those pointers in
    the `artifacts:` frontmatter field (a dash-list of "kind:target" entries; kind from the `artifact-kind`
    vocabulary in `wiki-page-spec`, where a `file:` entry takes a path relative to the project root to a file with no comment syntax
    and no original in a design tool), scaffolded commented below —
    uncomment and fill when a pointer exists (optional). A component reference in a file with comment
    syntax names this page with `@prototypes`, and importable code that renders the built component
    cites it with `@realizes`; a component held in a design tool is linked with that tool's kind. A hosted
    component workbench is no `artifacts:` kind: link its story or controls in the page text (States, Props / API)
    where one exists; a story that is code is not linked, because the code cites this page. Document
    the component to design-system component-doc completeness; iOS vs Android control idioms and visual
    deltas are Platform-variations prose in THIS page, never separate component pages or design systems.
  Columns: Decisions — Decision | State | Decided; Open questions — Question | Owner | Resume condition.
  Extra frontmatter: `status` (draft | preview-candidate | preview | stable) is REQUIRED — the component's
    lifecycle status, so the page is itself in a state: draft and preview-candidate are partly complete
    and in discovery, preview is mostly complete and usable in production, stable is complete across
    design, code and documentation, and the design kit where the system has one.
    `realizes` is REQUIRED — the feature(s) or module this page realizes; a page
    that serves the system generally rather than one module realizes `[[product:app-base]]`
    instead (see [[_authoring:wiki-page-types]]).
    `invalidates` (OPTIONAL) — dash-list of [[<domain>:<path>]] naming the live pages this decision
    makes partly stale; update each in the same change. Targets must be living pages — a record is
    superseded whole via `superseded-by` instead.
  Disposition: keep every header; "None." when empty.
  Substitute: {{TITLE}} {{DATE}} {{CONFIDENCE}} {{ORIGINATION}} {{STATUS}}.
-->

## Purpose & usage
<!-- What the component is and the problem it solves. When to use it — and, just as important, when
     NOT to (the adjacent component to reach for instead). A composition of components solving a recurring
     interaction problem is an interaction pattern (the `design-system`'s Interaction patterns), and how a page
     arranges its regions is a `layout-pattern`; neither is a component. One short paragraph plus do/don't bullets. Open with the page's lead sentence — see [[_authoring:wiki-authoring-spec#lead-sentence]]. -->

## Anatomy
<!-- The component's parts/slots (container, label, icon, affordances), each required or optional, and how
     they compose. Where a design-tool frame, story or project design file holds the visual anatomy,
     record it in the `artifacts:` frontmatter field (linked, never copied; that source stays canonical
     for the visual). -->

## Variants
<!-- The variant matrix — the dimensions along which the component varies (type, size, emphasis,
     tone…) and the valid combinations, every size and content configuration included. A small table works well. -->

## Tokens & measurements
<!-- The color, type and spacing tokens each part uses, per variant and size, and the annotated spacing
     and alignment. Name tokens the system defines (a design [[design:catalogs/<token-group>]] page or the
     design-system foundations section), never raw values; a value with no fitting token is a gap in the
     token set, recorded under `## Open questions`. -->

## States
<!-- The interaction/display states: default, hover, focus, active, selected, disabled, read-only, error,
     warning, loading — whichever apply. Note the visual treatment of each, or link the hosted workbench story that shows one.
     Loading keeps its own treatment: the control blocks a repeat activation at full strength, never the
     disabled dimming. -->

## Props / API
<!-- The configurable contract, when an implemented component is documented: the props/inputs, their
     types, defaults, and required vs optional. Every user-visible string is a prop; a prop is deprecated
     before it is removed or renamed. Link the hosted workbench's controls where one exists. "None documented yet."
     if the component is design-only so far. -->

## Behavior & interaction
<!-- The interaction model: what it does on activation, keyboard support, focus management, and any
     motion; and how it behaves under its content and container — responsiveness, overflow or reflow,
     expansion, scrolling. Describe behavior, not a specific framework's event API. -->

## Accessibility
<!-- The accessibility contract: role/semantics, keyboard operation, ARIA where needed, focus order,
     what a screen reader announces in each state, contrast, color never the only signal, and target
     size — per WCAG and the design accessibility principles. -->

## Platform variations
<!-- Per-platform deltas: iOS vs Android control idioms, native navigation patterns, and visual deltas
     the design system carries as one component — never separate pages or design systems. -->

## Content guidelines
<!-- How text in the component should read: labeling conventions, truncation/overflow behavior, and
     internationalization considerations (text expansion, RTL). Follow the project's UX-writing
     standard and the design system's Voice and tone ([[design:design-system#voice-and-tone]]; with none
     recorded, the standard's defaults hold and the gap goes under `## Open questions`) rather than
     restating style rules here. -->

## Decisions
<!-- Component design decisions and their rationale — the variant/API/interaction calls made and why,
     each citing the analysis or study that informed it — a `domain/comparisons/<slug>` bake-off via
     `[[domain:comparisons/<slug>]]`, or a usability test or variant prototype of our own surfaces
     recorded as a `design` `study` via `[[design:studies/<slug>]]`. A component decision lives here,
     not in a standalone `adr` (engineering-only). The register's states, the backing an `adopted` call names, and the `invalidates:` duty follow [[_authoring:wiki-page-state#decisions-registers]]. -->

| Decision | State | Decided |
|---|---|---|
| <the call> | proposed / adopted | |
